purpose: Per-tool acceptance for project-owned persistent environments. Each row states what was exercised and HOW STRONG the evidence is, so nothing reads as verified because a mock agreed with itself.

evidenceLevels.real-guest: Exercised against a real rootless Podman container in an exclusively created private store.
evidenceLevels.unit: Exercised against in-process fakes only. Proves the logic, not that the guest behaves this way.
evidenceLevels.unverified: No acceptance yet at any level, or only indirect coverage.

rows.capability: source publication preserves mode and relative symlinks
snapshot id mapping and retention pruning
project MCP install, reconnect, schema visibility
rows.notes: An earlier version of this row claimed the capability did not exist; that was wrong. A stdio server created while a managed project is selected is bound to it (projectRef, immutable) within the existing personal/instance scopes, and every connect, tools/list and call runs inside that project's guest on an mcp lease. Proven against a real guest with a dependency-free stdio fixture written into /workspace: AddMcpServer binds and discovers the tool through the guest, ReconnectMcpServer bridges it, the bridged call reports the container's hostname and a guest-only file, no lease survives the call. Negatives: the same bridged tool refuses from another project without touching the provider, a non-member is denied at the project boundary, the central host reconnect path refuses a bound server, and removal leaves no server process in the guest. Schema visibility is per owner scope, not per project: a bound tool is declared in every session of its scope and refuses at execution from the wrong project.

rows.capability: scheduled turn scoping to a managed project
delegated scope cannot retarget or enumerate projects
a managed conversation refuses its turn when no provider resolves
rows.notes: Observed for real when a stale bundled plugin made the whole sandbox control unresolvable.

rows.capability: Git and publishing credential separation
rows.notes: The guest exec unit carries only PATH, LANG and its own systemd bookkeeping; daemon environment sentinels including GH_TOKEN are absent. The other half of separation is a gap rather than a pass: no account GitHub token reaches a managed guest at all, so authenticated git push from a managed project is not supported.

rows.capability: codebase indexing/search inside a managed project
rows.notes: Indexed through the provider's guest file operations (list/read) and keyed by the project's stable id (managed:<projectId>), never by /workspace, which every project shares; before this the index resolved /workspace against the host and then merely refused. Embedding stays central (the guest never sees provider credentials); a search re-checks membership through environmentFor before reading any chunk; host sessions, admin all-access included, never see managed rows; the scheduled indexer skips managed keys because a timer has no acting member; project removal prunes the rows. Real guest: reindex walks and reads the guest, search answers with guest-relative paths, an unchanged workspace costs no reads or embeddings, a non-member is denied at the project boundary, the host path guard is never consulted. Cost: one guest operation per directory listed and per 256 KiB read, each several seconds on this host, so a first index of a large project is slow and bounded by the 20,000-file cap rather than by the embedding budget.

rows.capability: central personal integrations (onedrive, github, voice-bot, image-gen, image-edit, todo, stats, skills, web)
rows.notes: Central personal integrations do not read project files and have no managed path; listed as the record that they were reviewed and found out of the environment boundary, not as work left undone.

rows.capability: another project's identity cannot reach this environment
rows.notes: Denied at the project boundary, not by the file simply being absent.

rows.capability: a path the guest protocol cannot express safely is refused
rows.notes: The container is the boundary, so a guest path is not refused merely for sitting outside /workspace.

rows.capability: in-page download handling in a guest
rows.notes: A click-triggered download settles in /data/browser/downloads and reads back byte-exact through the provider.

rows.capability: office preview converters in a guest
rows.notes: The project image now ships libreoffice-writer/calc/impress, so the managed preview runs soffice inside the guest: a docx uploaded through the editor's own upload route comes back as a PDF from the preview route, and the converter's scratch directory does not survive the request. A non-office file is refused with 415. An environment created from an earlier image keeps its root filesystem until rebuilt and still answers 501 naming the missing converter (unit: editorManagedOperations). Cost: a conversion takes tens of seconds end to end on this host because each guest operation, not only soffice, costs several seconds.

rows.capability: ShareImage resolves a managed guest path
rows.notes: Shares the managed helper with ShareFile but was not driven against a real guest; listed separately rather than claimed by association.

rows.capability: conversation transcripts and tool-result spills under a managed project
rows.notes: Transcripts are central storage and have no guest side. The guest-side piece is the tool-result spill, which writes into the environment's artifact prefix and is covered by managedColdClearing and managedDeliverySpill. Not promoted to real-guest: driving it needs a full live session rather than a tool caller.
